prod/slow: Multiplying long numbers by hand is slow, and easy to get wrong. Adding them is quick.
prod/napier: In 1614, John Napier published tables of logarithms to trade one for the other. With them, he wrote, adding does the work of multiplying, and subtracting the work of dividing.
prod/curve: To see why, go back to the curve of e to the x, where ln reads a height back to its x.
prod/two: The curve reaches height two at x of about zero point six nine: that is ln two.
prod/three: Height three, at about one point one: that is ln three.
prod/six: Lay those two lengths end to end: zero point six nine plus one point one is one point seven nine. The curve there stands at six, which is two times three.
prod/why: It has to: two is e to the zero point six nine, three is e to the one point one, and multiplying exponentials adds their powers.
prod/rule: So for positive numbers a and b, ln of a b is ln a plus ln b. The log of a product, what multiplying gives, is the sum of the logs, one log per factor.
pow/nine: Nine is three times three, so its x is two equal steps of one point one: ln nine is about two point two.
pow/k: Any power is equal factors: a to the k is k factors of a. So its log is k equal steps: ln of a to the k is k times ln a.
pow/front: The power comes down in front, as a multiplier. It does not square the log: ln three, squared, is only about one point two one.
quot/half: Dividing undoes multiplying, so along x it steps back. Two times a half is one, which sits at zero, so the steps for two and for a half cancel: ln of a half is minus ln two.
quot/flip: One over a number flips the sign of its log: ln of a half is about minus zero point six nine.
quot/quot: So three divided by two steps back from ln three: one point one minus zero point six nine is zero point four one, the height one and a half.
quot/diff: The log of a quotient, what dividing gives, is the difference of the logs, top minus bottom: ln of a over b is ln a minus ln b.
quot/small: Any number p between zero and one sits left of zero, so minus ln p is positive: how far left it sits.
quot/order: The smaller p, the farther left, and the bigger minus ln p. Minus ln of zero point nine is only about zero point one one.
quot/try: Try one. Use ln two is about zero point six nine and ln five is about one point six one. Let p be a tenth. What is minus ln p?
quot/ten: A tenth is one over ten, so minus ln p is ln ten itself.
quot/solve: And ten is two times five, so add: zero point six nine plus one point six one is two point three oh.
